newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to sell 30 pct of Iberia to industry, banks.
newsitem.headline: Spain to sell 30 pct of Iberia to industry, banks.

text.p: Spain's state holding company SEPI, which controls flag carrier Iberia, said in an interview published on Sunday that around 30 percent of the airline would be sold to industrial and financial groups.
Following the announcement of preliminary agreements with British Airways and American Airlines on an alliance, SEPI said the two airlines would first take stakes in Iberia.

"The next step (after that) will be to place around 30 percent between industrial and financial groups," SEPI's chairman Pedro Ferreras said in an interview published in the newspaper El Mundo on Sunday.
"Another 10 percent will be in the hands of workers, and the rest will be launched on the bourse," he added.
Industry Minister Josep Pique said earlier in the week the government aimed to float around 50 percent of Iberia by the end of 1999.
SEPI sources said BA and American would take minimal stakes in the Spanish airline following the alliance.
Ferreras said the new alliance would prompt a fall in rates. "The primary beneficiary of this deal will be the consumer," he said.
